newsitem.title: USA: Sun Sportswear to merge with BSI.
newsitem.headline: Sun Sportswear to merge with BSI.

text.p: Sun Sportswear Inc said it had signed a defintive agreement to merge with BSI Holdings Inc and create one of the leading character apparel licensees in the United States.
Under the terms of the agreement, Sun stockholders other than Seafirst Bank will receive $2.20 per share in cash for 50 percent of their shares, it said.
They will retain the remaining 50 percent of their shares, subject to the right to choose to keep 100 percent of their shares and forgo the cash payment, it added.

Seafirst, which owns 3.8 million shares or 66.1 percent of the outstanding common stock, will have 48.3 percent of its shares exchanged for $2.20 per share in cash and a convertible promissory note, Sun Sportswear said.
Seafirst will retain its remaining shares, subject to adjustment based on what the other shareholders decide to do, it said.
The merger, which is structured as a tax-free exchange of shares, is expected to be completed by February 28, 1997, it added.

All of the shares of BSI, which makes and disrtibutes decorated sportswear, will be converted into shares of Sun common stock, representing about 88 percent of Sun's outstanding shares, Sun Sportswear said.
